IR.rationale: Rising intermediate yields relative to the policy rate signal a tightening repricing that hits the duration of HY and EM sovereign bonds and can persist over several weeks.

B.rationale: A credit sell-off, with spreads widening and HY returns weak, raises the expected credit risk premium. Partial reversal of these overshoots predicts higher subsequent returns.

V.rationale: High equity implied volatility proxies for elevated risk aversion and risk premia, which are associated with higher subsequent risky-bond returns.

AP.rationale: Strong recent equity excess returns signal compressed risk premia and some cross-asset reversal, which lowers the subsequent credit return.

ST.rationale: Strong momentum-factor performance marks crowded trend-following positioning in a calm regime, which tends to precede lower risky-asset carry returns.

FX.rationale: Dollar strength tightens global dollar funding and EM financial conditions, depressing returns on USD-denominated EM sovereign and HY debt.

COM.rationale: Broad commodity strength supports commodity-exporting EM sovereigns and energy/materials HY issuers through better cash flows and terms of trade.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions indicate funding stress that tends to persist over short horizons and weigh on credit returns.

ENDG.rationale: Credit-bond indices show short-horizon return autocorrelation from stale pricing and slow-moving flows.

IR.rationale: A repricing of the near-term policy path toward tightening raises rate uncertainty, which spills into credit-spread and duration volatility.

B.rationale: Joint weakness in HY and EM bonds signals a broad credit sell-off. Through the leverage effect and forced-selling dynamics, this raises future variance.

V.rationale: Implied volatilities that are elevated across equity and safe-haven gold markets signal broad, forward-looking uncertainty beyond what realised credit variance already captures.

AP.rationale: Simultaneous declines in US and EM equities indicate a global risk-off episode that typically precedes higher credit volatility.

ST.rationale: Outperformance of profitable firms reflects flight to quality, a sign of rising concern about weak balance sheets and therefore higher credit volatility.

FX.rationale: Sharp dollar appreciation tightens dollar funding for EM borrowers and leveraged firms, raising the volatility of USD credit.

COM.rationale: Commodity price falls stress energy HY issuers and commodity-exporting sovereigns, raising the variance of their bonds.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions reduce dealer balance-sheet capacity and liquidity, which amplifies credit-market volatility.

ENDG.rationale: Volatility is persistent and partly mean-reverting, so a high recent realised variance carries residual information about the next period.

IR.rationale: Bear steepening, with long yields rising relative to short ones, inflicts duration losses on long-dated EM sovereign and HY bonds.

B.rationale: Credit-stress states, with spreads widening and HY falling, can cascade through redemptions and forced selling into tail losses.

V.rationale: Elevated safe-haven and equity implied volatility signals heightened crash risk and a fatter left tail.

AP.rationale: Weak EM equities foreshadow capital outflows from EM, which hit sovereign USD debt and global risk appetite.

ST.rationale: A quality rally signals flight to safety and rising default concerns.

FX.rationale: Dollar surges tighten global funding conditions and are associated with EM debt sell-offs.

COM.rationale: Precious-metal rallies reflect safe-haven demand or inflation and real-rate shocks, both of which raise the risk of large losses on risky USD bonds.

MC.rationale: Joint tightness in financial conditions and elevated stress indices mark fragile markets prone to tail losses.

ENDG.rationale: Large credit losses cluster in time, so weak recent returns raise the chance of further extreme losses.

IR.rationale: Falling intermediate yields relative to the policy rate, reflecting expected easing or a rates rally, produce duration-driven gains.

B.rationale: After credit sell-offs, wide spreads and high risk premia set up sharp relief rallies, so the right tail fattens.

V.rationale: High implied volatility widens the whole return distribution and marks high risk premia, so large rebounds become more likely.

AP.rationale: Strong EM equity returns signal inflows to EM and improving risk appetite, which spill over to EM sovereign and HY debt.

ST.rationale: Momentum crashes occur during junk rebounds after stress, which coincide with sharp rallies in low-quality credit.

FX.rationale: A weakening dollar eases global funding conditions and supports strong gains in EM and HY USD debt.

COM.rationale: Oil rebounds sharply improve the credit outlook of energy HY issuers and oil-exporting sovereigns.

MC.rationale: Tight financial conditions mean depressed prices, from which policy responses or relief can trigger large gains.

ENDG.rationale: Extreme weekly gains often follow drawdowns as prices partially reverse liquidity-driven overshoots.
